subject: BrightCart POC: model criteria, evaluation plan & ops roadmap
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@brightcart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: BrightCart POC: post-demo recap + asks

Alex — great to meet earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

- Goal: 1) reduce self-serve checkout abandonment by surfacing contextual assistance and 2) automate policy-based product QA for new SKUs.
- Success metrics you called out: improve assisted-conversion by >=6 percentage points in targeted cohort; reduce manual QA time by 40% for new listings.
- Data constraints: customer PII stays in BrightCart environment; we will run trial on a dedicated dataset that you provide; no training on customer data.

Proposed POC scope (high level): 3-week trial, two endpoints: customer-facing assistant (low-latency) + batch product QA job (throughput-oriented).

Immediate asks for us to finalize the SOW & evaluation plan: 1) confirm success metrics and priority (assistant vs QA), 2) confirm Spanish coverage requirement for assistant (you mentioned Latin America traffic), 3) agree on trial kickoff window (we recommended week of Sep 28).

I attached a draft POC SOW and a short evaluation rubric to this email for speed. If that looks good, we’ll lock owners and calendar the kickoff.

Thanks,
Dylan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(d) +1 415-555-0123
Dylan@redwood.com

From: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@brightcart.com>

Cc: Natalie Park <natalie.park@brightcart.com>, procurement@brightcart.com
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BrightCart POC: post-demo recap + asks

Thanks Dylan — recap looks right. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- Priority: assistant use-case is higher priority (converts more traffic) but we want both in scope; if we must narrow, pause QA batch.
- Metrics: for assistant, target is +6pp conversion for targeted cohort and median latency < 250ms for 95th pct; for QA, target is 40% time savings.
- Spanish: yes — we need Spanish (es-MX & es-419) support for the assistant.

Procurement (cc’d) will need a simple SOW + estimated run card (tokens/day, concurrency) to move forward. Also want to discuss which open models you recommend for the assistant vs QA workload — we prefer open models (no vendor lock).

Can you add a short model recommendation section to the SOW and a preliminary cost/latency estimate?

Alex
Head of Product — Conversational, BrightCart
alex.gomez@brightcart.com
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@brightcart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BrightCart POC: post-demo recap + asks

Alex — good questions. I pulled our SRE/solutions notes into the SOW and added a model recommendation appendix (attached SOW v1.1). TL;DR recommendation for trial: 

- Assistant (primary): Llama2-13B-chat (quantized 4-bit, Redwood-verified config) — balance of instruction-following + latency on 1x A10 / 1x A100 equivalent.
- Assistant (fallback): Mistral-instruct-7B quantized 4-bit for sub-100ms low-cost short-turn queries (greetings, price lookup).
- Batch QA: Mistral-7B / Falcon-7B local quantized variant for high-throughput scoring.

Spanish strategy: use primary model for bilingual prompts; we’ll include a small locale-conditioned prompt template and augment with light pre-translation step for edge cases. If Spanish traffic is >30% of requests during trial we’ll evaluate a dedicated es-tuned variant and fallback to translation pipeline.

Proposed timeline: 
- Sep 28: kickoff (1 hour) — confirm dataset access + security checklist.
- Week 1 (Sep 29–Oct 5): environment setup, model runtime configs, baseline latency/cost smoke tests.
- Week 2 (Oct 6–Oct 12): evaluation runs, collect rubric metrics.
- Week 3 (Oct 13–Oct 19): iteration & handoff + final acceptance.

Owners: 
- Sales/POC lead: Dylan Brooks (me)
- Solutions/infra: Marissa Cole (SE)
- Customer success: Ben Carter (CS)

I attached an updated SOW and the evaluation rubric csv. Also included a quick run-card estimate for a 3-week run (tokens/day, average concurrency) — rough numbers only. Please confirm and we’ll route the updated SOW to procurement for sign-off.

Dylan
--

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BrightCart POC: model criteria, evaluation plan & ops roadmap

Hi Alex/Dylan — quick technical notes to set expectations for the trial and evaluation rubric: 

- Latency: 95th pct <250ms is achievable for short-turn assistant prompts on Llama2-13B with 4-bit quantization if we tune sequence length and KV-cache reuse. Long instruction templates (>=1024 tokens) will push latency higher; recommend capping assistant prompt context to 512 tokens for latency-sensitive paths.
- Throughput: batch QA jobs should run on quantized 7B variants; expect ~150–200 samples/sec on a single A100 when batched appropriately.
- Cost controls: enable prefix caching for frequent help dialogs, and route fallbacks for heavy retrieval queries to smaller model.
- Evaluation: we’ll measure conversion-lift (A/B cohort), response relevance (human-rated 1–5), hallucination rate on a seeded set, latency percentiles, and token cost per accepted response. I added these to the rubric.

Action items for BrightCart before kickoff: 
1) Provide a 2k-row sample of assistant logs (anonymized) + 500 product SKUs for QA job.
2) Confirm if we can run trial in your VPC (preferred) or on Redwood Hosted.
3) Point procurement to SOW v1.1 for execution.

Happy to jump on a 30-min technical pre-kickoff if you want to walk through the eval rubric.

—Marissa
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Natalie (procurement) — looping you in to coordinate the SOW and SOW signature cadence.

Alex
